mainTopic: Preparing and choosing the grain for the עומר, wormy flour and wood, and the best sources of oil for מנחות
overview: The amud opens by settling how the field for the עומר is plowed. The משנה and a ברייתא seem to disagree, but they speak about two kinds of fields, and a second ברייתא shows that the field is plowed in both years. רבי יוחנן and אבא שאול teach that the עומר came from sunny southern fields, farmed half at a time, and רב חלקיה בר טובי's field proves the method works. Next the גמרא rules that mostly wormy flour or wheat is פסול, and it does the same for wormy altar wood, with שמואל limiting that rule to wet logs. רבא's questions about getting מלקות for consecrating these wormy items end in תיקו. A new משנה names תקוע as the best source of oil and lists which olives may not be used. The גמרא links תקוע's oil to wisdom, then tells a long story about a plain-looking farmer in אשר's land who had enough oil to fill a giant order, fulfilling 'and dips his foot in oil.' At the end, the גמרא returns to the משנה and begins a challenge about unripe olives that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Only the ברייתא says to plow a second time
steps.stepSummary: The challenge ends by pointing out that only the ברייתא, not the משנה, says the plowing is repeated.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only the ברייתא that teaches 'he repeats' the plowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a challenge that started earlier: the משנה does not mention plowing twice, but the ברייתא does. So it looks like the two sources disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes plowing in the first year and sowing in the second, with no second plowing. The ברייתא adds the word שונה, meaning the plowing is done again. The question is whether the משנה and the ברייתא really argue about this.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
Repeats; here, plows the field a second time

phrases.english: It is the baraita that teaches "he repeats."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a challenge that began before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה and the ברייתא agree about how the field for the עומר is prepared
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה leaves out a second plowing, but the ברייתא requires one. That suggests the two sources disagree.

steps.title: Two different kinds of fields
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה speaks about a field that was already worked, and the ברייתא speaks about a field that was not worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. Here it speaks about a worked field, and there it speaks about a field that is not worked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the two sources are talking about different situations, so they do not argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A field that has already been worked is soft enough, so one plowing is enough, as in the משנה. A field that was not worked needs a second plowing, as in the ברייתא. The disagreement disappears because each source deals with its own kind of field.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult; the opening of an answer
Here... there; splitting two sources into two cases
A field that is not worked (uncultivated)

phrases.english: This is not difficult;
here, it is about a worked field,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the משנה, which needs only one plowing.

phrases.english: there, it is about a field that is not worked.
phrases.notes: "There" means the ברייתא, which says to plow again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא disagree about whether a second plowing is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: They do not disagree. A worked field needs one plowing, and a field that was not worked needs two.

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the final conclusion is on this question.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion on this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the final answer about plowing the field for the עומר. This sets up the next step, where it brings a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last answer only showed that the sources can agree. It did not tell us what is actually done in practice. So the גמרא now asks for a clear conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the conclusion on this?; asking for the final ruling

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from answering the challenge to asking for the practical ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the field for the עומר is plowed again in the second year

steps.title: Plow half, sow half, each year
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the field is plowed in the second year as well, before sowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it is taught: He plows half and sows half; he plows half and sows half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא that describes plowing and sowing in each of the two years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "plows... and sows" is repeated for the second year. That shows that plowing comes before sowing in the second year too. So the conclusion is that the field is plowed again.
steps.whatToRemember: The conclusion is that the field for the עומר is plowed in the second year as well, before it is sown.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught in a baraita:
he plows half of it and sows half of it,
phrases.notes: One way to read this: in the first half of the year he plows the whole field, then sows only half of it.

phrases.english: he plows half of it and sows half of it.
phrases.notes: This is the second year. He plows again, then sows the half that was left empty last year.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא: נָר חֶצְיָהּ וְזוֹרֵעַ חֶצְיָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא repeats "plows... sows" for the second year, which shows the field is plowed again before sowing.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The field is plowed in both years.

steps.title: The עומר comes only from the sunny southern fields
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that the עומר is brought only from the southern fields of ארץ ישראל, which get sun all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The עומר is brought only from the southern fields of ארץ ישראל, since the sun rises on them and sets from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי יוחנן about where the barley for the עומר should come from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Southern fields get sunlight from sunrise to sunset. That much sun grows the best grain. So רבי יוחנן limits the עומר to these fields.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the sixteenth of ניסן

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
One does not bring the omer
except from the southern fields
that are in Eretz Yisrael,
for upon them the sun rises,
and from them the sun sets.
phrases.notes: He means these fields are in the sun all day long, from morning until evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵין מְבִיאִין אֶת הָעוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: where the עומר comes from
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עומר is brought only from the southern, fully sunlit fields of ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the southern field and describes how it was farmed
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול teaches that the עומר came from a sunny southern valley called בית מקלה. It was farmed by plowing and then sowing only half the field each year.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this. אבא שאול says: the עומר came from the valley of בית מקלה. The field was about three סאה in size. It was a southern field, and the sun rose on it and set on it. Each year the farmer plowed it and then sowed half of it. The next year he plowed again and sowed the other half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבי יוחנן's statement that the עומר came from a southern field that gets sun all day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מודרמת' (southern) and 'the sun rises and sets on it' match what רבי יוחנן said. The ברייתא also adds new practical information: the field was rested in alternating halves, so each part was strong when it was sown.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח
The valley of בית מקלה, where the עומר grain was grown
A measure of volume, also used to measure a field's size

phrases.english: This is also taught in a ברייתא:
Abba Shaul says:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹמֶר הָיָה בָּא מִבִּקְעַת בֵּית מִקְלָה,
phrases.english: The omer would come from the valley of Beit Mikle,
it was about three se'a,
phrases.notes: This is the field's size: an area big enough to sow about three סאה of seed.

phrases.english: and it was a southern field,
and the sun would rise upon it
and the sun would set from it.
He plows for half and sows half,
phrases.notes: He plows during the first half of the year, then sows only half the field and leaves the other half resting.

phrases.english: he plows for half and sows half.
phrases.notes: The next year he does the same thing, but now he sows the half that rested.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's statement from Step 5
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that the עומר comes from southern fields that get sun all day
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting אבא שאול about the field in בקעת בית מקלה

steps.title: רב חלקיה בר טובי's field shows how well the method works
steps.stepSummary: רב חלקיה בר טובי farmed his land by plowing and sowing half at a time. It yielded double and produced wheat fine enough for סולת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חלקיה בר טובי had a piece of land. He plowed it and sowed half, then plowed it and sowed the other half. It produced twice as much, and he sold the wheat for fine flour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story showing that the half-and-half farming method really works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story adds real-life proof to the ברייתא's description. Resting each half of the field doubled the crop and made the wheat good enough for fine flour (סולת).

keyTerms.meaning: A corner or tract of land
Two for one, meaning double the usual crop

phrases.english: Rav Chilkiya bar Tovi
had a tract of land,
he plowed for half and sowed half,
he plowed for half and sowed half,
and it produced two for one,
and he would sell the wheat for fine flour.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִלְקִיָּה בַּר טוֹבִי הֲוָה לֵיהּ קַרְנָא דְּאַרְעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example of the farming method from Step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plowing and sowing half the field at a time doubled the crop and gave wheat of fine-flour quality.
steps.whatToRemember: The עומר field was southern and sunny, and it was farmed half at a time to give the best grain.

steps.title: Wormy flour or wheat is unfit when most of it is wormy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that wormy flour is פסולה. A ברייתא explains that flour or wheat is פסול when most of it has become wormy.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if it became wormy, it is unfit. The Rabbis taught: fine flour that is mostly wormy is unfit, and wheat that is mostly wormy is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה about wormy flour and brings a ברייתא that defines when it becomes unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets the standard at 'most' (רוב). It applies this both to flour that is already ground and to whole wheat kernels. The next step will ask what exactly 'most of the wheat' means.

keyTerms.meaning: Fine flour used for a מנחה
Unfit for use in an offering

phrases.english: And if it became wormy, it is unfit.
The Sages taught:
Fine flour most of which became wormy is unfit,
and wheat most of which became wormy is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה: wormy flour
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flour or wheat that is mostly wormy is פסול for a מנחה.

steps.title: Does 'most' mean most of each kernel or most of the whole סאה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks whether the wheat is פסול when most of a single kernel is wormy, or when most of the kernels in a סאה are wormy. The question is left unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asks: does 'most' mean most of one wheat kernel, or most of a סאה of wheat? The question stands unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks what the ברייתא means by 'most of the wheat,' and the גמרא cannot settle it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One reading: if most of a single kernel is eaten by worms, that kernel is פסול. The other reading: only when most of the kernels in a whole סאה are wormy is the whole סאה פסול. The גמרא ends with תיקו, meaning no answer was found.

keyTerms.meaning: He asks, raising a question that needs an answer
Let it stand. The question stays unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the question was wrong. It means the גמרא could not find a clear answer, so the question stays open.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asks:
Is it the majority of a single wheat kernel,
or the majority of a se'a?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what 'most' means in the ברייתא from Step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'most' refers to most of a single kernel or most of the kernels in a סאה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: None. The question ends in תיקו.

steps.title: Is someone who consecrates wormy wheat punished like one who consecrates a blemished animal?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether someone who is מקדיש wormy wheat gets מלקות under the ban on consecrating a בעל מום, or whether that ban covers only animals. The question is left unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asks: if someone consecrated wormy wheat, does he get lashes for it because of the rule against consecrating a blemished thing? Since the wheat is unfit, maybe it counts like a blemished animal. Or maybe 'blemished' applies only to an animal. The question stands unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks whether the punishment for consecrating a blemished animal also applies to wormy wheat, and the גמרא leaves it unresolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side says the wheat is פסול, so it is just like a בעל מום animal, and he should get מלקות. The other side says the idea of a בעל מום only exists for animals, so there is no מלקות for wheat. The גמרא ends with תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: He consecrated them, setting them aside for the בית המקדש
A blemished animal, unfit to be an offering

steps.whatToRemember: Mostly wormy flour or wheat is פסול. Two follow-up questions stay unresolved (תיקו): what 'most' means, and whether consecrating wormy wheat brings מלקות like a בעל מום.

phrases.english: Rava asks:
If he consecrated them,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the wormy wheat kernels from the previous step.

phrases.english: what is the law: is he lashed for them
because of the rule about a blemished one?
phrases.notes: There is a prohibition against consecrating a blemished animal as an offering, and it is punished with lashes.

phrases.english: Since it is unfit, it is like a blemished animal,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא אֵין בַּעַל מוּם אֶלָּא בִּבְהֵמָה?
phrases.english: or perhaps 'blemished' applies only to an animal?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question building on the rule that wormy wheat is פסול
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the מלקות for consecrating a בעל מום applies to wormy wheat or only to animals
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: None. The question ends in תיקו.

steps.title: A log with a worm is unfit for the altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from another מסכת: any log found to have a worm in it is פסול for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: any log in which a worm is found is unfit for use on the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: Having just discussed wormy flour, the גמרא now brings a related משנה about wormy wood. This sets up שמואל's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic of worms ruining something meant for the מזבח moves from flour to the firewood burned on the מזבח. The rule as quoted sounds absolute: any worm makes the log פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: A log of wood, here the firewood for the מזבח

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת מדות, which talks about checking the wood for the altar.

phrases.english: Any log in which a worm is found
is unfit for the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from wormy flour (steps 8 to 10) to a parallel case of wormy wood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A log with a worm in it is פסול for the מזבח.

steps.title: שמואל limits the rule to wet wood
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the משנה only means wet wood. A dry log can be scraped clean and is then כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל says: They only taught this about a wet log. But a dry log, he scrapes it and it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains the משנה from the last step and narrows it. Only wet wood with a worm is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In wet wood the worm damage cannot simply be removed. In dry wood the wormy spot can be scraped off, and what remains is good wood. So the משנה's rule really applies only where the damage cannot be fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about... (a phrase that limits a rule)

phrases.english: Shmuel says:
They taught this only about a wet log,
but a dry one, he scrapes it and it is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the משנה quoted in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only wet wormy wood is פסול. Dry wood is scraped and is then כשר.

steps.title: Is one flogged for consecrating a wormy log?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether someone who is מקדיש a wormy log gets מלקות because of the ban on consecrating a בעל מום. The question is left as תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asks: If one consecrated it, is he flogged for it because of the ban on a blemished offering? Since it is unfit, is it like a blemished animal? Or perhaps a בעל מום applies only to an animal? Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks the same question about wormy wood that the גמרא already asked about wormy wheat in step 10. It stays unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two sides. The log is פסול, so maybe it counts like a blemished animal, and consecrating it would bring מלקות. Or maybe the ban on consecrating a בעל מום only applies to animals, so wood is not included. The גמרא cannot decide.

keyTerms.meaning: He consecrated it (set it aside for the מקדש)
It is like a blemished animal

phrases.english: Rava asks: If he consecrated it,
phrases.notes: "It" here means the wormy log from the last step.

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ שֶׁיִּלְקֶה עָלָיו מִשּׁוּם בַּעַל מוּם?
phrases.english: is he flogged for it because of the ban on a blemished offering?
Since it is unfit, is it like a blemished animal?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא אֵין בַּעַל מוּם אֶלָּא בִּבְהֵמָה?
phrases.english: Or perhaps the ban on a blemished item applies only to an animal?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָבָא: הִקְדִּישׁוֹ, מַהוּ שֶׁיִּלְקֶה עָלָיו מִשּׁוּם בַּעַל מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the question of step 10, now about wood instead of wheat.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ban on consecrating a בעל מום, which carries מלקות, extend to an unfit log, or only to animals?
steps.whatToRemember: Two questions are left as תיקו: whether consecrating wormy wheat or wormy wood brings מלקות as a בעל מום.

steps.title: משנה: תקוע is the best source of oil
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה says תקוע is the top source of oil for מנחות. אבא שאול says רגב, east of the ירדן, is second. Every region was valid, but oil was brought from these places.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: תקוע is first for oil. אבא שאול says: second to it is רגב across the ירדן. All the lands were valid, but they would bring it from here.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. Earlier the משנה listed the best places for flour, and now it lists the best places for oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a ranking of quality, not a rule about what is allowed. The משנה says outright that oil from any region is כשר. These places were simply chosen because their oil was the best.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה: the start of a new משנה
First, the best (like the letter alef)
Tekoa, a town known for its olive oil
The east side of the Jordan River

phrases.english: MISHNA: Tekoa is first for oil.
Abba Shaul says: Second to it
is Regev, across the Jordan.
All the lands were valid,
but it was from here that they would bring it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה, moving from flour to oil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oil from any region is כשר. The best came from תקוע, and the second best from רגב.

steps.title: Olives to avoid, and olives that are unfit
steps.stepSummary: Oil should not be taken from fertilized groves, irrigated groves, groves with grain sown between the trees, or unripe olives, but if it was brought it is כשר. Oil from olives that were soaked in water, pickled, or boiled is פסול even after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not bring oil from a fertilized grove, an irrigated grove, or a grove sown with grain between the trees. If he did bring it, it is valid. One may not bring oil from unripe olives. If he did, it is valid. One may not bring oil from olives soaked in water, pickled, or boiled. If he did, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues and sorts olives into two groups. Some olives should be avoided but still work after the fact. Others never work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fertilizer, watering, crowding the trees, and picking too early all lower the oil's quality, but it is still real olive oil. That is why it stays כשר after the fact. Soaking, pickling, or boiling actually changes the olive itself, so oil from those olives is פסול even if it was already brought.

keyTerms.meaning: A grove that was fertilized with manure

steps.confusionAlert: "אין מביאין" (one may not bring) appears in both groups, but the endings are opposite. In the first two groups, "if he brought it, it is כשר." In the last group, "if he brought it, it is פסול." Always check the ending.
steps.whatToRemember: Poorer-quality olives are avoided but still כשר after the fact. Olives that were soaked, pickled, or boiled are פסול even after the fact.

phrases.english: One may not bring oil from a fertilized grove,
nor from an irrigated grove,
nor from a grove where grain was sown between the trees,
but if he did bring it, it is valid.
One may not bring oil from unripe olives,
but if he did bring it, it is valid.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְבִיאִין מִן הַגַּרְגְּרִין שֶׁנִּשְׁרוּ בְּמַיִם,
phrases.english: One may not bring oil from olives that were soaked in water,
nor from pickled olives,
nor from boiled olives,
and if he did bring it, it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, moving from where the oil comes from to which kinds of olives can be used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oil from fertilized groves, irrigated groves, groves sown with grain between the trees, and unripe olives is avoided but כשר after the fact. Oil from soaked, pickled, or boiled olives is פסול even after the fact.

steps.title: Why did יואב go to תקוע for a wise woman?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק where יואב brings a wise woman from תקוע and asks why he chose that town.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'And יואב sent to תקוע and took from there a wise woman.' What is special about תקוע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting a פסוק about תקוע, the town the משנה named as the best source of oil. It then asks why יואב picked that town in particular.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just said תקוע has the finest oil. The גמרא connects this to another place where תקוע shows up in תנ״ך. The question sets up an answer that will link the two.

keyTerms.meaning: A town, named in the משנה as the best source of oil for מנחות
What is different / what is special about

phrases.english: GEMARA:
"And Joab sent to Tekoa,
and took from there a wise woman."
What is special about Tekoa?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה from Step 14, which named תקוע as the top source of oil.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why יואב specifically chose תקוע to find a wise woman.

steps.title: Olive oil brings wisdom
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the people of תקוע regularly use olive oil, and so wisdom is common among them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Since they are used to olive oil, wisdom is common among them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. תקוע had wise people because they were used to olive oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties the פסוק back to the משנה. תקוע is the town of the best oil, and that same oil is the reason it was known for wise people. So יואב went to the place where wisdom was easy to find.

keyTerms.meaning: They are used to (it); it is common for them
Wisdom is common / easy to find

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Since they are used to olive oil,
wisdom is common among them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁרְגִילִין בְּשֶׁמֶן זַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Olive oil was a regular part of life in תקוע, and this made wisdom common there.

steps.title: אשר's land flows with oil
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains משה's blessing to אשר, 'and dips his foot in oil,' as describing how oil flows in אשר's portion like a spring.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'And dips his foot in oil.' This is the portion of אשר, which draws oil like a spring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stays with the subject of oil-rich places and brings a ברייתא. It explains a פסוק from משה's ברכה to אשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says אשר will 'dip his foot in oil.' The ברייתא reads it as a picture of how much oil there is in אשר's land: it pours out like water from a spring. The story that follows will show this literally.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And dips his foot in oil', from משה's ברכה to אשר

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"And dips his foot in oil":
this is the portion of Asher,
which draws oil like a spring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of oil-rich places, moving from תקוע to the portion of אשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה's blessing 'dips his foot in oil' describes how much oil flows in אשר's land, like a spring.

steps.title: לודקיא sends a messenger to buy oil
steps.stepSummary: The story begins: the people of לודקיא needed oil and sent a messenger to buy a huge amount, a million worth.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Once the people of לודקיא needed oil. They appointed a messenger and told him: Go and bring us oil worth a million.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts a story that will show how rich in oil אשר was. This step sets the scene: a city needs a huge amount of oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount, a million worth, is huge. The story will ask where anyone could find that much oil. That makes the ending, where one farmer has it all, more striking.

keyTerms.meaning: A messenger / agent sent on a mission

phrases.english: They said: Once,
the people of Laodicea were in need
of oil.
phrases.notes: Some versions have בְּשֶׁמֶן, in round brackets; the corrected wording is לְשֶׁמֶן, in square brackets. Either way, the meaning is the same.

phrases.english: They appointed a messenger for themselves,
and said to him: Go
and bring us oil worth one million.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: פַּעַם אַחַת נִצְרְכוּ לָהֶן אַנְשֵׁי לוּדְקִיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the story that shows the ברייתא's point about אשר's oil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup: a city needs an enormous amount of oil and sends a messenger to buy it.

steps.title: The search leads to a farmer hoeing his olive trees
steps.stepSummary: The messenger is sent from ירושלים to צור to גוש חלב, and finally to a man hoeing under his olive trees, who asks him to wait until he finishes working.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went to ירושלים; they said: go to צור. He went to צור; they said: go to גוש חלב. He went to גוש חלב; they said: go to so-and-so in that field. He found him hoeing under his olive trees. He asked: Do you have a million's worth of oil that I need? The man said: Wait until I finish my work. He waited until he finished.
steps.whatsHappening: The messenger is sent from place to place because no one has that much oil. In the end he is sent to a plain farmer working in his field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even big places like ירושלים and צור could not supply this much. The trail leads to גוש חלב and then to one man, which builds up the surprise. The farmer is in no rush and finishes his work first.

keyTerms.meaning: גוש חלב, a town where the trail leads to the farmer
Hoeing, loosening the soil around trees

phrases.english: He went to Jerusalem;
they said to him: Go to Tyre.
He went to Tyre;
they said to him: Go to Gush Chalav.
He went to Gush Chalav;
they said to him: Go to so-and-so,
to that field.
And he found him hoeing under his olive trees.
He said to him: Do you have
the million's worth of oil that I need?
He said to him: Wait for me
until I finish my work.
He waited until he finished his work.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָלַךְ לִירוּשָׁלַיִם, אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֵךְ לְצוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: the messenger's search for the oil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No major city could supply the oil; the search ends at a single farmer in his olive grove.

steps.title: The messenger thinks he is being mocked
steps.stepSummary: The farmer throws his tools over his back and clears stones on the way, so the messenger doubts he could be rich and thinks the Jews are making fun of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he finished his work, he slung his tools behind him and was clearing stones as he walked along the road. The messenger said: Do you really have a million's worth of oil? It seems to me the Jews are making fun of me.
steps.whatsHappening: The farmer acts like a simple poor worker. The messenger starts to think he was sent on a joke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything about the man looks poor: he carries his own tools and picks up stones as he walks. This sets up the surprise at the end, when the man's wealth is revealed.

keyTerms.meaning: He slung his tools (over his back)

phrases.english: After he finished his work,
he slung his tools behind him,
and was clearing stones as he went along the road.
He said to him: Do you have
a million's worth of oil?
It seems to me
that the Jews have made fun of me.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַחַר שֶׁסִּיֵּים מְלַאכְתּוֹ, הִפְשִׁיל כֵּלָיו לַאֲחוֹרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: the farmer's simple behavior makes the messenger doubt him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The farmer looks like a poor laborer, and the messenger suspects a prank.

steps.title: He dips his feet in oil, just as the פסוק says
steps.stepSummary: At home, his maid brings hot water and then a golden basin full of oil, and he dips his hands and feet in it, fulfilling 'and dips his foot in oil.'
steps.simpleTranslation: When he reached his city, his maidservant brought him a kettle of hot water and he washed his hands and feet. She brought him a golden basin full of oil and he dipped his hands and feet in it, to fulfill what is written: 'And dips his foot in oil.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches its big surprise: the plain farmer is so rich in oil that he dips his feet in it from a golden basin. This fulfills the ברייתא's reading of the פסוק, and the story continues in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man's wealth shows when he gets home: he has a maidservant, a golden basin, and so much oil that he uses it on his feet. This part of the story closes by quoting the same פסוק from Step 18. משה's blessing to אשר came true word for word.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא praises the oil-rich places: oil from תקוע brought wisdom, and אשר's land had oil like a spring. The story shows a simple-looking farmer who literally dipped his feet in oil, fulfilling משה's blessing.
steps.confusionAlert: The farmer looked poor, but that was the point of the story. People in אשר's land could be very wealthy in oil without showing it.

phrases.english: When he reached his city,
his maidservant brought out to him
a kettle of hot water,
and he washed his hands and feet with it.
She brought out to him a golden basin
full of oil,
and he dipped his hands and feet in it,
to fulfill what is said:
"And dips his foot in oil."
phrases.notes: דברים 33:24, the same פסוק the ברייתא opened with.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְעִירוֹ, הוֹצִיאָה לוֹ שִׁפְחָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reveals the farmer's wealth and ties it back to the פסוק from Step 18. The story then continues.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The blessing 'and dips his foot in oil' came true literally in אשר's land: even a plain farmer there had oil enough to bathe his feet in it.

steps.title: The farmer sells a huge amount of oil, and more on credit
steps.stepSummary: After the meal, the farmer measures out a million worth of oil. He then offers the messenger another 180,000 worth on credit and says he will come along to collect the payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: After they ate and drank, he measured out a million worth of oil for him. He asked: Do you need more? The messenger said: Yes, but I have no money. The farmer said: If you want it, take it, and I will go with you and collect the money. He measured out another 180,000 worth of oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The story keeps going. The farmer who looked poor turns out to have enough oil to fill the whole huge order and still more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The messenger thought the farmer was too poor to help him. Now the farmer fills the full order of a million and offers even more without asking for payment up front. This shows that his wealth was real, and that he trusted the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten thousand; מֵאָה רִיבּוֹא is a million
And I will collect its price

phrases.english: After they ate and drank,
he measured out for him oil worth a million.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: כְּלוּם אַתָּה צָרִיךְ לְיוֹתֵר?
phrases.english: He said to him: Do you need any more?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: הֵן, אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין לִי דָּמִים.
phrases.english: He said to him: Yes, but I have no money.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אִם אַתָּה רוֹצֶה לִיקַּח – קַח,
phrases.english: He said to him: If you want to take it, take it,
and I will go with you and collect its price.

phrases.aramaic: מָדַד לוֹ שֶׁמֶן בִּשְׁמוֹנָה עָשָׂר רִיבּוֹא.
phrases.english: He measured out for him oil worth 180,000.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after the farmer dips his hands and feet in a golden basin of oil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The farmer fills the million order and adds 180,000 more on credit.

steps.title: Every animal in the land was rented to carry the oil
steps.stepSummary: People said there was so much oil that the messenger rented every horse, mule, camel and donkey in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: People said: That man did not leave a horse, a mule, a camel or a donkey in ארץ ישראל that he did not rent.
steps.whatsHappening: The story describes how enormous the shipment was. It took every pack animal in the land to carry it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line shows the true size of the farmer's wealth. One plain-looking farmer had enough oil to need every animal in the country to move it.

phrases.english: They said: That man did not leave
a horse or a mule
or a camel or a donkey
in ארץ ישראל that he did not rent.
phrases.notes: "That man" is the messenger, who rented the animals to carry the oil home.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how big the shipment from step 23 was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The oil shipment was so large that every pack animal in the land was hired.

steps.title: Praise the farmer, not me: the verse is fulfilled
steps.stepSummary: Back home, people come out to praise the messenger. He tells them to praise the farmer instead, who sold him a million worth and lent him 180,000 more. This fulfills the פסוק about someone who looks poor but is very rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he reached his city, the people came out to praise him. He said: Don't praise me. Praise this man who came with me. He measured out a million worth of oil for me and is owed 180,000 by me. This fulfills the verse: 'There is one who acts rich but has nothing; one who acts poor but has great wealth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. The messenger gives the credit to the farmer, and the גמרא ties everything to a פסוק in משלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man the messenger thought was a pauper turned out to be hugely rich. The פסוק fits him exactly: he looked poor but had great wealth. The whole story shows how richly oil flowed in אשר's portion, as in step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: Is a creditor, is owed money
Acts as if he is rich
Acts as if he is poor

steps.whatToRemember: The story proves how plentiful oil was in אשר's land. A farmer who looked poor could supply a giant order. That is the meaning of 'and dips his foot in oil.'

phrases.english: When he reached his city,
the people of his city came out to praise him.
He said to them: Do not praise me,
but rather this man who came with me,
who measured out for me oil worth a million,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרֵי נוֹשֶׁה בִּי בִּשְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה רִיבּוֹא,
phrases.english: and look, I owe him 180,000,
to fulfill what is said:
"There is one who acts rich but has nothing,
one who acts poor but has great wealth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story begun in step 19 and ties it to a פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The farmer who looked poor was truly rich, which fulfills the פסוק and shows the oil-rich blessing of אשר.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: no oil from a fertilized grove
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves the story and returns to the משנה, quoting its rule that oil for a מנחה is not brought from a fertilized grove.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: One does not bring oil from a fertilized field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new section by quoting the משנה again. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story about אשר's oil is over. Now the גמרא goes back to the practical laws of which oil is fit for a מנחה. The first rule quoted is that oil from a fertilized grove is not brought.

keyTerms.meaning: A flour offering, which often has oil in it

phrases.english: One may not bring oil from a fertilized field,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the laws of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oil for a מנחה is not brought from olives of a fertilized grove.

steps.title: A ברייתא about unripe olives begins a challenge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to challenge the משנה with a ברייתא that says oil from unripe olives (אנפקטן) is not brought. The rest of the ברייתא continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: One does not bring oil of unripe olives...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a challenge by quoting a ברייתא. Only its first words appear here; the full challenge comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וְהָתַנְיָא' (but wasn't it taught) signals that a ברייתא is about to clash with the משנה's wording. The topic is oil from unripe olives. The problem will only become clear once the rest of the ברייתא is quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the answer yet. This step is only the opening of the challenge, and the ברייתא keeps going on the next amud.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: One may not bring oil from unripe olives,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a ברייתא to begin questioning the משנה's rules about which oil may be brought.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule about bringing oil from unripe olives
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא on the same subject is introduced with 'וְהָתַנְיָא,' which signals a clash. The exact contradiction appears when the rest of the ברייתא is quoted.
